entry.title: Two hands working on a bead
entry.summary: Davies describes threading as a way to explore what two hands can do together. Bead size and thread thickness follow the child’s ability, with an adult supervising small parts.
entry.cue: Your child may be interested in guiding a thread through a bead and finding it on the other side.
detail: Her illustrated threading example is from 16 months. In the appendix, the 16–18+ month row begins with five or six wooden beads and plastic tubing that can be pushed a little way through a bead.

Her chapter also describes a lace with a firm wooden end before an ordinary shoelace. These are different material examples; choose a manageable challenge rather than trying to follow every variation.
A child can repeat one small part, accept a slow demonstration, or leave it for another time. The later examples with small beads and thin thread are not a requirement to make this activity harder.
